text: so i was making this fence and [Image #6] it came out alright i guess but the part that took forever was the top when cutting out the faces and then re-facing the insides so that it was like a hole. im thinking there is likely a better approach than the 20 minutes it took me to do every single edge by hand lol
resolution: Same thread as req_1722 (the user's follow-up clarified the target was a chainlink style). Diagnosed why the fence-top holes took 20 min: the arch is a solid slab, and the toolkit had no inset/punch/hole op — extrudeFace only pulls a lip and solidifyFaces only walls holes on an already-open shell, so hand-cutting + re-facing each opening's inner walls was the only path. Resolved by building a parametric Lattice/grille primitive (latticePanel in editMesh.ts) that generates a thin walled panel full of openings from crossed bars, so the inner walls of every hole exist for free: 'grid' pattern = the fence-top slot band, 'diamond' = chainlink. Wired into the Add Shape dialog with pattern + openings/wire/frame/thickness controls; 4 new editMesh.test.ts suites green (101/101). See req_1722 for the full build paragraph.
